title: Predict how a signal's size changes through fifty layers
brief: Compute a layer's gain and the gain after many layers, then simulate a random stack and check the simulation against your prediction.
hints: layer_gain is n_in * scale**2. The scale is a standard deviation, so it is squared.
depth_gain raises the gain to the power depth. Multiplying gain by depth gives a straight line instead of the curve.

forward_variance: draw h first with rng.normal(size=(num_trials, widths[0])), then for each layer draw W with rng.normal(scale=scale, size=(widths[l], widths[l + 1])) and set h = h @ W. Record np.mean(h ** 2) before the first layer and after every layer.
In the relu branch, apply np.maximum(h, 0.0) right after the multiply, never to the input.
